messages:
kai: Heads-up — onboarding Hyperfoil's LoRA patch (merged into adapters/hyperfoil) and running int4 quant + structured sparsity. Pushed a quickpack of prompts to /evals/hyperfoil_quickpack. Seeing odd token-level sparsity artifacts where numeric fields get truncated sometimes. Anyone available to triage?

anya: On it. Can you paste the quickpack results or a sample prompt that reproduces the truncation?

kai: Sample prompt pasted below — occurs on invoice lines and amounts: 
```
Invoice: 
- Item A: $120.00
- Item B: $45.50
Total: $165.50

Prompt: "Summarize the invoice and return a JSON with items and total."
```
Output sometimes becomes: 
```
{"items": [{"name": "Item A", "price": "120"}, {"name": "Item B", "price": "45"}], "total": "165"}
```
(the .50 dropped)

ben: Re-ran the quickpack on int8 / int4 / fp16 variants. Quick summary: int4+structured-sparsity shows ~2.3% token-drop on currency microtokens vs fp16 baseline. int8 has ~0.6%. Seems quant+pruning interaction.

ben: Paste of the stripped-down eval metrics: 
```
model_variant, ppl, currency_microtoken_drop_rate, halluc_rate
fp16, 1.02, 0.1%, 0.5%
int8, 1.10, 0.6%, 0.7%
int4+sparse, 1.28, 2.3%, 1.6%
```

sophie: @kai do we have tokenizer mismatch or rounding code in the post-processor that might strip decimals? we should check token boundaries for ".50" tokens.

kai: Good call — hyperfoil adapter changes a tiny tokenizer-normalization mapping to coerce certain punctuation for legacy customer data. I reverted locally and re-ran: int4+sparse still shows ~1.5% drop (better but not gone). So both tokenization + quantization contribute.

eval-bot: quickpack run finished (run_id: qp-3276500000-1). Top regressions attached: 
- Decimal preservation: regression +1.7% (int4+sparse vs fp16)
- Numeric rounding hallucinations: +1.1%
- Structured JSON validity: fails increased from 0.4% -> 2.2%

lisa: Suggestion: 1) try loosening sparsity pattern (reduce prune ratio per-attention-head to 0.2) 2) run tiny targeted tests with token-level assertions (ensure ".50" preserved). I can patch the quickpack with 50 targeted examples.

anya: Also add a deterministic seed and run with kv-cache warm vs cold — some quant kernels have AK mismatch with cache that affects low-prob tokens.

kai: Thanks. I'll land a branch with reduced sparsity and the targeted 50 cases, run int4 again, and post results. If it still fails we'll fallback the customer's default route to int8 while we iterate.

ben: FYI — added a canary policy in routing: hyperfoil -> int8 by default for now. I'll monitor perf impact. :thumbsup:

kai: Updated results: int4+sparse (reduced prune) -> currency_drop 0.9%, JSON-fail 1.0%. Better but not baseline. Will follow up with more ablations tomorrow.

sophie: Good incremental progress. If we can reproduce with a minimal model snapshot, we can file an upstream kernel bug with runtime team.

lisa: I'll push the 50-case quickpack now. tagging @sophie for tokenizer checks.

kai: Thanks all — keeping this thread for follow-ups. If anyone notices other numerical microtoken issues for Hyperfoil, drop examples here. :eyes:
